adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:57 — Pre-existing: monitor_env.status is saved as ERROR before the incident get_or_create and the Kafka occurrence production, with no transaction wrapping them. If either later step throws, the env is left in ERROR with no incident, and every later failure takes the ERROR branch where active_incident is None, so no issue is ever raised until an OK check-in.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` the code sets `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` and persists it (`monitor_env.save(update_fields=("status",))`) before attempting `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(...)` and later producing occurrences (via `create_incident_occurrence`). There is no transaction/rollback protection shown. If the incident creation (or anything after the status save) raises, the environment can remain persisted in `ERROR` without an active incident. On subsequent failures, the `elif monitor_env.status == MonitorStatus.ERROR:` branch uses `incident = monitor_env.active_incident`, and occurrences are only produced when `incident` is truthy (`... and incident:`), so the diff-grounded risk of getting stuck in ERROR with no incident/occurrence is real.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:62 — Pre-existing: two concurrent failed check-ins can both read status OK after refresh_from_db and both run get_or_create(resolving_checkin=None) with no lock or unique guard. That can create two open MonitorIncidents, so later get_or_create/active_incident lookups can hit MultipleObjectsReturned or pick the wrong one.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), when `monitor_env.status` is `OK/ACTIVE` it unconditionally does `MonitorIncident.objects.get_or_create(monitor_environment=monitor_env, resolving_checkin=None, ...)` without any transaction/locking around the status transition (`monitor_env.status = ERROR; save()`) or around the `get_or_create`. The diff shows no unique constraint/guard ensuring only one `MonitorIncident` can exist with `(monitor_environment, resolving_checkin=None)`, so two concurrent callers could both observe `OK/ACTIVE` and both create an “open” incident row. That would make later lookups like `monitor_env.active_incident` potentially ambiguous (e.g., `MultipleObjectsReturned`).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:48 — Pre-existing: when fewer than failure_issue_threshold check-ins exist (e.g. a new ACTIVE monitor with threshold=5 and 1 failed check-in), the slice returns fewer rows, none of them OK, so an incident opens before the threshold is reached.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `incidents.py`), when `failure_issue_threshold > 1` it queries check-ins, slices `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]`, and then immediately checks only for presence of any `OK` statuses. If there are fewer than `failure_issue_threshold` rows (e.g., new monitor), `previous_checkins` will be shorter, contain no `OK`, and the code proceeds to set `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` and create an incident anyway. There is no guard like `if len(previous_checkins) < failure_issue_threshold: return False`, so the incident can open before the threshold is actually reached.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:59 — Pre-existing, now exposed as a standalone public API: try_incident_threshold does not guard threshold <= 0 itself (only mark_failed normalizes 0/None). A 0 or negative threshold gives an empty slice, and previous_checkins[0] raises IndexError after status was already saved as ERROR.

adjudication.rationale: In `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:try_incident_threshold`, when `failure_issue_threshold != 1` it slices `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]` and then immediately does `starting_checkin = previous_checkins[0]` after saving `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR`. If `failure_issue_threshold` is `0` or negative, the slice is empty, `any(...)` is false, status is saved as ERROR, and then `previous_checkins[0]` raises `IndexError`. There is no guard in `try_incident_threshold` against `<= 0` in the diff.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:102 — Pre-existing: in the ERROR branch, when active_incident is None the occurrence is skipped silently, yet monitor_environment_failed still fires and the function returns True, so a monitor stuck in ERROR with no incident fails with no issue produced.

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), the `MonitorStatus.ERROR` branch sets `incident = monitor_env.active_incident` and later only creates occurrences if `incident` is truthy (`if ... and incident:`). Regardless, it still sends `monitor_environment_failed` and returns `True`. So if `active_incident` is `None` while the env is in `ERROR`, the failure produces no occurrence and fails “silently” aside from the signal—this edge-case is real and diff-grounded, but it’s not clearly a newly introduced behavioral defect (the removed `mark_failed_threshold` code had the same pattern).

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:48 — When failure_issue_threshold > 1, nothing checks that len(previous_checkins) >= threshold, so a new monitor with fewer failed check-ins than the threshold (e.g. its first check-in fails with threshold=3) opens an incident early (pre-existing boundary bug, moved verbatim)

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` when `failure_issue_threshold > 1`, `previous_checkins` is built from a queryset and then sliced: `previous_checkins = list(reversed(previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]))`. If there are fewer than `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins, this slice will be shorter (possibly length 1). There is no subsequent check that `len(previous_checkins) >= failure_issue_threshold` before setting `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` and creating an incident using `starting_checkin = previous_checkins[0]`. Therefore a monitor with fewer failures than the threshold can still open an incident early, matching the finding.

adjudication_records.issue_text: src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py:52 — The threshold window only excludes OK check-ins, so IN_PROGRESS check-ins count as failures toward the threshold and get an occurrence each, which can open an incident before enough real failures happen (pre-existing)

adjudication.rationale: In `try_incident_threshold` (new `src/sentry/monitors/logic/incidents.py`), the threshold logic builds `previous_checkins` from *all* check-ins up to `failed_checkin.date_added` (`MonitorCheckIn.objects.filter(...).values("id", "date_added", "status")`) and only aborts if any have `status == CheckInStatus.OK` (`if any([checkin["status"] == CheckInStatus.OK ...]): return False`). That means any non-OK status (e.g., an in-between/non-failure status) will be treated as contributing toward the failure threshold, potentially triggering `monitor_env.status = MonitorStatus.ERROR` and creating an incident earlier than intended. Additionally, occurrences are produced for every check-in in `previous_checkins` (`for checkin in checkins: create_incident_occurrence(...)`), regardless of whether each status is a real failure type.
